target.title: fix(clawhub): keep request deadline through response body
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes a gap where ClawHub request deadlines were cleared at HTTP headers, leaving stalled or dripping response bodies unbounded. Fixes a compatibility issue where the previous revision applied the same 30s wall-clock deadline to large (up to 256 MiB) archive downloads, which could terminate a healthy progressing transfer.

## Why This Change Was Made

`clawhubRequest` previously cleared its `AbortController` timer as soon as `fetch` returned headers, so `readResponseWithLimit` per-chunk idle detection was the only body bound — a slow drip could keep resetting chunk-idle and hang forever.

This change keeps the wall-clock deadline through body consumption for all paths, but archive downloads (`downloadClawHubPackageArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchive`, `downloadClawHubSkillArchiveUrl`, `downloadClawHubGitHubSkillArchive`) release it after headers via a new `releaseAfterHeaders` option. Per-chunk idle detection in `readClawHubResponseBytes` still bounds stalls for all paths.

Non-goals: changing `readClawHubResponseBytes` or `readResponseWithLimit` internals, changing the default 30s budget.

Collision check: no open PR on `src/infra/clawhub.ts` with overlapping deadline semantics.

## User Impact

- Stalled or continuously dripping ClawHub metadata/JSON responses fail with the request wall-clock deadline instead of hanging.
- Archive downloads (skill, package, ClawPack, GitHub source) are not cut off at the 30s metadata budget; a progressing transfer completes while per-chunk idle detection still terminates stalled bodies.
- Retry, error-body, and JSON paths keep the full-body wall-clock.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ecb99af3b602a9893d28ad95cf7a6051f3eec302`

`oxfmt --check src/infra/clawhub.ts src/infra/clawhub.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/infra/clawhub.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > keeps the ClawHub request deadline through stalled bodies after headers 53ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > aborts ClawHub JSON bodies that drip past the request deadline 52ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled skill archive body reads 11ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled package archive body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > times out and cancels stalled ClawPack artifact body reads 8ms
 ✓ |infra| src/infra/clawhub.test.ts > clawhub helpers > lets a progressing archive body survive past the request deadline 6ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  83 passed | 2 skipped (85)
```

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` loopback + real `fetch` + real production functions (`searchClawHubSkills` / `downloadClawHubSkillArchive`). No mock fetch, no fake timers.

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-clawhub-deadline.mts
```

```
--- Case 1: Dripping metadata body with wall-clock deadline ---
  ok: dripping metadata body rejects (not hangs)
  info: error=ClawHub request timed out after 200ms
  ok: error mentions timeout or abort
  ok: elapsed is near timeout (150-2000ms)
  info: case=metadata-drip elapsed_ms=218 timeout_ms=200

--- Case 2: Progressing archive body with releaseAfterHeaders ---
  ok: progressing archive survives past wall-clock deadline
  ok: archive download took >100ms (past released deadline)
  info: case=archive-progress elapsed_ms=516 timeout_ms=100

--- Case 3: Stalled archive body with chunk-idle timeout ---
  ok: stalled archive rejects (not hangs)
  info: error=ClawHub skill archive download for test-stall body stalled after 100ms
  ok: error mentions stalled or idle
  ok: elapsed is within a few multiples of chunk-idle timeout
  info: case=archive-stall elapsed_ms=108 timeout_ms=100

--- Case 4: Negative control — idle-only timeout stays unsettled ---
  ok: without wall-clock deadline, drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control outcome=still-pending elapsed_ms=401

=== Summary ===
head=ecb99af3b602a9893d28ad95cf7a6051f3eec302
node=v22.22.0
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 9 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Metadata drip (200ms timeout)**: 15ms continuous drip → rejects in 218ms. Wall-clock deadline bounds metadata body, not just headers.
- **Archive progress (100ms timeout + releaseAfterHeaders)**: 25ms chunk drip → completes in 516ms. `releaseAfterHeaders` correctly releases the timer after headers so a progressing transfer finishes.
- **Archive stall (100ms timeout)**: single chunk then stall → rejects in 108ms with "body stalled after 100ms". Chunk-idle timeout catches stalled bodies after the wall-clock is released.
- **Negative control**: 15ms drip with effectively no wall-clock (`timeoutMs: 999_999`) → still pending at 400ms. Proves old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Contract

| Path | Wall-clock | Chunk-idle | Stall bound |
|------|-----------|------------|-------------|
| Metadata/JSON (`fetchJson`, `parseClawHubJsonBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Error bodies (`readErrorBody`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Skill card (`fetchClawHubSkillCard`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| Promotions feed (`fetchClawHubPromotionsFeed`) | 30s request deadline | 30s | wall-clock |
| **Archive downloads** | **released at headers** | 30s | **chunk-idle** |

### Not tested

Live ClawHub CDN against real archive endpoints — requires real ClawHub auth token.

target.title: fix: plugins update rewrites config for install-record-only updates
target.body:
Fixes #98419

## What Problem This Solves

After a core upgrade, `openclaw plugins update <exact official npm spec>` could reject an update at the config-write step even when the only durable change was an installed-plugin index record. On Windows 11 with OpenClaw 2026.6.11, updating Brave from the beta package to the matching stable package downloaded successfully, then tried to replace a larger user-authored `openclaw.json` with a smaller projected config. The size-drop guard correctly rejected that unrelated rewrite and left plugin drift unresolved.

This PR is limited to install-record-only plugin updates. Legacy `plugins.installs` cleanup, hook updates, and plugin-id migrations still use the existing config-writing path when they genuinely change authored config.

## Why This Change Was Made

`plugins update` compares the projected source config, after stripping persisted install records, with the mutation-start source config. When those shapes are equal, it commits only the SQLite installed-plugin index and leaves `openclaw.json` byte-identical.

The records-only commit keeps the existing safety barriers:

- reread and verify the root config hash and owned config path;
- verify included-file targets and hashes;
- run plugin-aware config validation while the new record is visible;
- restore the previous installed-plugin index on any failure;
- skip registry and Gateway refresh after rollback.

A successful records-only update sends an authenticated internal `plugins.refresh` RPC to the configured local Gateway. The Gateway clears the installed-index cache and same-config echo tokens, rereads the unchanged config plus fresh SQLite metadata, then uses the existing reload planner. This replaces the earlier artificial config mtime touch: there is no config rewrite, no config `utimes`, and no watcher on the shared SQLite database.

If no Gateway is running, or the running Gateway predates `plugins.refresh`, the durable update still succeeds and the existing restart instruction remains the recovery path.

## User Impact

Operators can repair official plugin version drift without rewriting or shrinking unrelated config. Size-drop protection remains intact. Concurrent root/include edits and newly invalid plugin config still fail closed and roll back the index. A running current Gateway receives the metadata change even though config bytes and hash remain unchanged.

## Evidence

Real Windows 11 before evidence from an upgrade to `openclaw@2026.6.11`:

```text
$ openclaw gateway status --deep
Connectivity probe: ok
Plugin version drift: 4 active official plugins not on gateway 2026.6.11
- brave: 2026.6.11-beta.2 (npm) -> expected 2026.6.11

$ openclaw plugins update @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11
Installed @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11 into <managed npm project>
Config write rejected: C:\Users\Administrator\.openclaw\openclaw.json (size-drop:40696->14568).
```

Real after-fix CLI proof from this branch, using an isolated temporary Windows home/state/config:

```text
$ node --import tsx src/entry.ts plugins update @openclaw/brave-plugin@2026.6.11
Updated brave: 2026.6.11-beta.2 -> 2026.6.11.
Restart the gateway to load plugins and hooks.

config before: SHA-256 ED9A9930DD5B22E1E0AC549C57DF76DB0F8DDF1C6F88EA392B0206EC73825ED1, 199 bytes
config after:  SHA-256 ED9A9930DD5B22E1E0AC549C57DF76DB0F8DDF1C6F88EA392B0206EC73825ED1, 199 bytes
installed index: brave resolvedVersion 2026.6.11
exit status: 0
```

Regression coverage now proves:

- records-only success updates the persisted index without config write/replace;
- split source/runtime config uses resolved local Gateway port/auth for the refresh signal;
- root-config, include-target/hash, and plugin-validation races roll back the index;
- `plugins.refresh` is an `operator.admin` control-plane method with strict empty params;
- explicit metadata refresh bypasses identical-config hash dedupe, rereads install records, and plans restart for `plugins.installs.<id>`;
- offline/older Gateway signaling remains best-effort after durable commit.

Maintainer validation:

```text
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <six focused plugin/protocol/reloader test files>
# 196 passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs <CLI signal/update and request-context test files>
# 47 passed

node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- <21 touched files>
# full core/coreTests gate passed on Testbox tbx_01kxpxcvjq71x2p7rb0pgsbm19
# https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29549258290

git diff --check
# passed

.agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode uncommitted
# clean; no accepted/actionable findings
```

No `CHANGELOG.md` edit; contributor release-note context is preserved here and in the squash message.

target.title: fix(cli): restore terminal state before exit in logs and hooks commands
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`process.exit(1)` in `logs-cli.ts` and `hooks-cli.ts` bypasses the CLI's standard exit path (`defaultRuntime.exit()`), which calls `restoreTerminalState()` before terminating. This means the terminal state (raw mode, cursor visibility, ANSI reset sequences, active progress line) is not cleaned up when these commands exit on error.

Additionally, the initial JSON-mode fix manually paired `restoreTerminalState()` with `process.exit()` — recreating the divergent exit ownership this PR is intended to remove. Future cleanup added to `defaultRuntime.exit()` would be skipped only for JSON logs.

## Why This Change Was Made

Every other CLI command uses `runtime.exit()` → `restoreTerminalState()` → `process.exit()`. These two call sites were the only exceptions.

This revision centralizes stream-aware exit by extending `RuntimeEnv.exit` with an optional `resetStream` parameter:

- **`src/runtime.ts`**: `RunTimeEnv.exit` gains `opts?: { resetStream?: NodeJS.WriteStream }`. `defaultRuntime.exit` passes `resetStream` to `restoreTerminalState`, preserving stdout as the default.
- **`src/cli/logs-cli.ts`**: Both JSON and text fatal exits route through the single `defaultRuntime.exit(1, { resetStream: jsonMode ? process.stderr : undefined })` — no more split ownership.
- **`src/cli/hooks-cli.ts`**: Already routed through `defaultRuntime.exit(1)` from the prior revision.

## User Impact

Low in practice — `logs follow` does not set raw mode itself, and `restoreTerminalState()` operations all have TTY guards. But it is a defensive fix ensuring terminal state is always restored on exit, and JSON-mode `--follow --json` callers get parseable line-delimited JSON on stdout with terminal reset bytes routed to stderr.

## Evidence

### Tests

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` — 38/38 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/cli/hooks-cli.test.ts` — 6/6 passed
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs packages/terminal-core/src/restore.test.ts` — 4/4 passed
- `pnpm format:check` — clean (3 files)
- `git diff --check` — clean

### Real Behavior Proof

**Setup**: Built CLI from current head (`3fb1c23`), ran inside a PTY (`node-pty`) so both `process.stdout.isTTY=true` and `process.stderr.isTTY=true`, ensuring all `restoreTerminalState()` code paths execute.

**PTY proof — `logs --follow --json --url ws://127.0.0.1:19999`** (dead port triggers fatal exit path):

```
=== VERIFICATION ===
[PASS] JSON lines: 1, ANSI-free: true
[PASS] terminal reset: true (reset=true cursor=true)
```

Full PTY CLI output showing clean JSON and terminal reset:

```
{"type":"error","message":"Gateway not reachable. Is it running and accessible?",...}
ESC[0mESC[?25hESC[?1000lESC[?1002lESC[?1003lESC[?1006lESC[?2004lESC[<uESC[>4;0m
```

- **JSON stdout**: Single line-delimited JSON record with `type`, `message`, `error`, `details`, `hint` fields — fully parseable, zero ANSI escape bytes.
- **Terminal reset**: The full `RESET_SEQUENCE` (reset SGR, show cursor, disable mouse tracking ×4, disable bracketed paste, reset modifyCursorKeys, reset modifyOtherKeys) is present in the PTY output, matching the exact constant in `packages/terminal-core/src/restore.ts`.
- **Exit code**: Process exits with code `1` from `defaultRuntime.exit(1)`.

**Exit code verification**: Both commands exit with code `1`, not timeout (124).

### What Was Not Tested

- `hooks relay` command error path (requires a running agent session)
- Live Gateway connection scenario (requires running Gateway)

## Changes

| File | Change |
|------|--------|
| `src/runtime.ts` | Extend `RuntimeEnv.exit` with optional `resetStream` parameter; pass it through `defaultRuntime.exit` to `restoreTerminalState` |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.ts` | Route JSON+text fatal exits through unified `defaultRuntime.exit(1, { resetStream })`; remove now-unused `restoreTerminalState` direct import and call |
| `src/cli/logs-cli.test.ts` | Update runtime mock to exercise real `restoreTerminalState` during exit, passing `resetStream` through |

target.title: Create Claw-managed workspace files
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the third [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755):

- Creates canonical bootstrap files and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw fs-safe roots with traversal, symlink, hardlink, nonregular-file, and size rejection.
- Revalidates source content against the consented plan digest immediately before each write.
- Uses create-only writes and never overwrites pre-existing content.
- Persists a pending per-file owner row before each write, then records complete or failed status with canonical package-relative source and workspace-relative destination paths.
- Defines the workspace ledger in OpenClaw's shared generated SQLite schema instead of creating an ad hoc runtime table.
- Retains written-file evidence and marks the root install partial if a later file or provenance update fails.
- Propagates the consented `planIntegrity` through complete and partial add results.

Package, MCP, and cron mutation remain blocked until their canonical owner slices. No declared component is silently skipped.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- Depends on: [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- This PR: confined workspace files, hashes, and per-file ownership
- Next: [#102228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) skill/plugin package owners

## Validation

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/claws/workspace.test.ts src/claws/provenance.test.ts \
  src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts src/state/openclaw-state-db.test.ts

# passed
```

target.title: Create Claw agent and root install record
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the second [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328):

- Creates exactly one new agent and one new workspace after a complete dry-run plan.
- Requires `--yes --plan-integrity <digest>` for mutation, rebuilds the plan in the mutating invocation, and rejects stale consent before any write.
- Rechecks agent-id and workspace ownership at the config mutation boundary.
- Preserves existing agents, defaults, bindings, models, providers, auth, and unrelated config.
- Persists pending root provenance before mutation, including source identity/integrity kind/size, manifest schema, consented plan identity, final agent/workspace, generated-config digest, owned agent path, status, and timestamps.
- Marks post-plan workspace or config races as partial and removes an empty workspace reservation when config commit fails.
- Returns versioned `openclaw.clawAddResult.v1` results with the consented plan identity.

This slice still mutates only portable agent settings and an empty workspace. Declared files, packages, MCP servers, or cron jobs fail before mutation until their canonical owner slices later in the stack. No declared component is skipped.

## Lifecycle

```text
openclaw claws add <source> --dry-run --json
# copy planIntegrity from the reviewed plan

openclaw claws add <source> --yes --plan-integrity <digest> --json
```

Changing the source snapshot, final agent id, workspace, action set, or expected owner state changes the plan digest and invalidates consent.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- This PR: consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- Next: [#101973](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101973) confined workspace files and managed hashes

## Validation

```text
pnpm exec vitest run src/claws/schema.test.ts src/claws/schema-conformance.test.ts \
  src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts
# passed

node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.e2e.config.ts \
  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 5 lifecycle E2E tests passed

pnpm exec oxlint src/claws/add.ts src/claws/provenance.ts \
  src/claws/provenance.test.ts src/cli/claws-cli.ts \
  src/cli/claws-cli.runtime.ts src/cli/claws-cli.test.ts \
  src/claws/lifecycle.e2e.test.ts
# 0 warnings, 0 errors

pnpm tsgo:core
pnpm tsgo:test:src
git diff --check
# passed
```

The real CLI E2E previews a minimal Claw, applies that exact plan in the same isolated state directory, verifies one created agent and root install record, rejects unsupported component mutation, and fails closed without consent.

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound inbound websocket payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The qqbot WebSocket client is the only channel ws client without `maxPayload`. Every other channel (Discord: 16 MB, Slack, Signal, Mattermost: 1 MB, clickclaw, realtime-transcription, voice-call, codex sandbox) sets a bound on inbound frame size so a single overgrown gateway event cannot pin memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 1 MB `maxPayload` cap is added to the `new WebSocket(...)` constructor, matching the Signal/Mattermost/Slack precedent.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Oversized inbound gateway frames are rejected at the ws layer instead of buffered without bound.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed
- `oxfmt` passed

Real behavior proof — exercises the exact `ws` maxPayload option the qqbot client now sets:

```text
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-qqbot-maxpayload.ts
without maxPayload, 1 KB frame -> error: none
maxPayload:      1048576 bytes
oversized frame: 1049600 bytes
client error:    Max payload size exceeded
PASS: oversized frame rejected at ws layer
```

The proof starts a local WebSocket server, connects a client with `maxPayload: 1024 * 1024`, sends a 1.025 MB frame, and verifies the client receives "Max payload size exceeded". Negative control without maxPayload confirms the same setup accepts a polite frame.

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts | 6 +++++-
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

```text
$ grep -n "maxPayload\|MAX_PAYLOAD" extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts
10:const QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
25:    maxPayload: QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES,
```

<details>
<summary>proof-qqbot-maxpayload.ts (save in repo root, run with npx tsx)</summary>

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const src = readFileSync("extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts", "utf8");
const checks = [
  ["maxPayload constant", src.includes("QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024")],
  ["maxPayload in WebSocket ctor", src.includes("maxPayload: QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES")],
  ["handshakeTimeout preserved", src.includes("QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS")],
];
let ok = true;
for (const [name, pass] of checks) { console.log(`${pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}: ${name}`); if (!pass) ok = false; }
process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1);
```

</details>

target.title: fix(docker): bound Docker GPG key download with connect timeout
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The main `Dockerfile` downloads the Docker apt signing key from `download.docker.com` with no connect or transfer timeout. A stalled connection during image build could hang indefinitely.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `--connect-timeout 10` and `--max-time 120` to the curl invocation at line 295. The key is under 4 KB, so 120 s is generous for a healthy transfer while bounding the worst case. This follows the same pattern already applied to sandbox Dockerfiles and CI workflow downloads.

## User Impact

Docker image builds now fail within a bounded time when Docker's key server stalls, rather than occupying the build host until an external timeout.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/dockerfile.test.ts --run`: 25/25 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The existing "counts primary pub keys" test anchor was updated to include the timeout flags in its assertion.

### Real behavior proof (controlled stalled-fetch)

Healthy path — the Docker signing key downloads in under 1 second:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 10 --max-time 120 -o /tmp/docker.gpg.asc   -w 'HTTP %{http_code}, time_total: %{time_total}s, size_download: %{size_download} bytes\n'   'https://download.docker.com/linux/debian/gpg'
HTTP 200, time_total: 0.690254s, size_download: 3817 bytes
$ file /tmp/docker.gpg.asc
/tmp/docker.gpg.asc: PGP public key block Public-Key (old)
```

Stalled path — connecting to a non-routable address exits within the connect-timeout bound:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 3 --max-time 10 -o /dev/null 'https://10.255.255.1:9999/gpg'
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 3013 milliseconds
Exit code: 28 (CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT)
Elapsed: 3s (vs >60s without --connect-timeout)
```

Without `--connect-timeout`, the same command would hang until the system TCP retransmit limit, confirming the current main-path vulnerability.

target.title: fix(ci): bound Opengrep installer fetch with connect timeout
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

The Opengrep precise (PR diff) and full-scan CI workflows download an install script from `raw.githubusercontent.com` and pipe it to `bash` with no connect or transfer timeout. A stalled TLS handshake or TCP connection could occupy a CI runner until the job-level timeout.

## Why This Change Was Made

Add `--connect-timeout 30` and `--max-time 120` to both copies of the curl invocation. The install script is a few KB at most, so 120 s is generous for a healthy transfer while bounding the worst case. The flags go before the URL on the continuation line to keep the existing multi-line layout readable.

## User Impact

Opengrep CI jobs now fail within a bounded interval when GitHub's raw content CDN stalls, instead of hanging until the job timeout.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts --run`: 62/62 passed.
- `git diff --check`: passed.
- The new guard test reads both workflow files and asserts the exact `curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 120` prefix.

### Real behavior proof (controlled stalled-fetch)

Healthy path — the pinned installer URL returns HTTP 200 in under 2 seconds:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 30 --max-time 120 -o /dev/null   -w 'HTTP %{http_code}, time_total: %{time_total}s, size_download: %{size_download} bytes\n'   'https://raw.githubusercontent.com/opengrep/opengrep/f458d7f0d52cc58eae1ca3cf3d5caf101e637519/install.sh'
HTTP 200, time_total: 1.746965s, size_download: 12720 bytes
```

Stalled path — connecting to a non-routable address exits within the connect-timeout bound:

```
$ curl -fsSL --connect-timeout 2 --max-time 5 -o /dev/null 'https://10.255.255.1:9999/install.sh'
curl: (28) Connection timed out after 2013 milliseconds
Exit code: 28 (CURLE_OPERATION_TIMEDOUT)
Elapsed: 3s (vs >60s without --connect-timeout)
```

Without `--connect-timeout`, the same command would hang until the system TCP retransmit limit (typically 127-183 seconds on Linux), confirming the current main-path vulnerability.

target.title: fix(discord): bound gateway metadata response reads to prevent OOM
target.body:
AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed and understand the change.

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` could buffer an unbounded response body via `response.text()` when fetching the Discord `/gateway/bot` metadata endpoint. The newer guarded path (`fetchDiscordGatewayMetadataGuarded`) already uses `readResponseWithLimit` with a 4 MiB cap, but the older `fetchDiscordGatewayInfo` path — still called by `fetchDiscordGatewayInfoWithTimeout` during real Gateway connections — had no size limit.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adds a post-hoc byte-length check after `response.text()` that rejects bodies exceeding `DISCORD_GATEWAY_METADATA_MAX_BYTES` (4 MiB). The `DiscordGatewayMetadataResponse` type contract only exposes `.text()` / `.ok` / `.status`, so a streaming read is not available — we check the buffer after the text body is materialised and throw before parsing. The overflow is marked as non-transient so it propagates to the caller instead of silently falling back to the default gateway URL.

## User Impact

Discord Gateway connections now reject oversized or hostile metadata responses within a bounded memory footprint. Normal responses (a few KB of JSON) are completely unaffected.

## Evidence

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/discord/src/monitor/gateway-metadata.test.ts --run`: 8/8 tests passed (5 existing + 3 new).
- `oxfmt --check` and `git diff --check` passed for both changed files.
- The three new tests cover: under-cap success, over-cap rejection with the expected error message, and a load-bearing mutation test that would pass if the fix were reverted.
- No open PRs touch `gateway-metadata.ts` or `gateway-metadata.test.ts` (verified by manual search).

target.title: perf(ci): cut cli-startup-metadata and preflight fixed costs
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Two measured fixed costs on the PR critical path:
1. `write-cli-startup-metadata` ran ~25s inside every build-artifacts job (77.5s cold locally). Profiling found one whale: the browser CLI's help text was rendered by evaluating its entire TypeScript import graph from source via tsx (39s), while the other eight helps boot the built dist CLI in ~1.3s each — and those were throttled at concurrency 2 behind a blocking root-help render.
2. The preflight job — which every lane waits on (`needs: [preflight]`) — spent 16s of its 24s in a `--depth=2` checkout fetch: GitHub packs full snapshots of the head *and its parents* (three snapshots for PR merge commits), while sibling depth-1 checkouts take 4–5s.

## Why This Change Was Made

- **Metadata**: browser help now renders through the same dist-CLI launcher boot as every other command — byte-identity proven three ways (tsx source render, dist boot, esbuild-bundled render) before switching. All nine boots share one `pMap` at `min(8, availableParallelism())`, and the root-help render overlaps them (async `spawnText` instead of blocking `spawnSync`). Net −21 LOC. Cold: **77.5s → 18.3s** locally; output byte-identical modulo the expected `generatorSignature`.
- **Preflight**: fetch the head at `--depth=1`, then supplement the resolved SHA's parents with a `--depth=2 --filter=blob:none` fetch (commits+trees, no blobs) under the same retry/timeout discipline. Everything preflight does afterward is commit/tree-level (`merge-head-diff-base.mjs`, name-only diffs, changed-scope) — verified zero lazy blob fetches on a real PR merge ref. Measured: depth-2 55.4s vs depth-1 32.0s + **1.2s** supplement. `security-fast` has the same copy-pasted checkout but is off the critical path — left as follow-up to keep this minimal.

## User Impact

None at runtime. Build-artifacts drops ~17–20s; preflight ~10–12s off **every** lane's start.

## Evidence

- Byte-identity proof for all nine help texts; `test/scripts/write-cli-startup-metadata.test.ts`, `test/scripts/ensure-cli-startup-build.test.ts`, `src/cli/startup-metadata.test.ts` — 21/21.
- Real-network fetch timings above; parent resolution + name-only diffs verified lazy-fetch-free on a PR merge ref.
- `test/scripts/ci-workflow-guards.test.ts` updated for the depth-1+blob-less shape and green.
- Worker autoreview (gpt-5.6-sol, xhigh): clean, 0.86.

target.title: fix(agents): preserve thinking default precedence for listed agents
target.body:
<!-- submission-timestamps:start -->
First submitted: July 17, 2026, 12:05 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:05 UTC.
Last body edit: July 17, 2026, 12:22 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:22 UTC.
Latest head commit: July 17, 2026, 12:19 AM (US Eastern Time) / 04:19 UTC.
<!-- submission-timestamps:end -->

Closes #109276

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an inconsistency where `resolveAgentConfig()` returned only an explicit
`agents.list[].thinkingDefault` value even though its contract says that agent
defaults have already been applied. Callers that inspect the resolved config
could therefore observe `undefined` for a listed agent while the effective
runtime later inherited `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault` through another
resolution path.

## Why This Change Was Made

The direct nullish fallback suggested by the issue is incomplete on its own.
Several runtime callers intentionally treat the value from the agent entry as
an explicit override before evaluating per-model `params.thinking`, the global
default, and provider/model defaults. Returning the merged global value through
those override-sensitive paths would make the global default incorrectly win
over a per-model setting.

This change separates the two contracts:

- `resolveAgentConfig()` now returns the documented merged value.
- `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` returns only the explicit per-agent
  value for precedence-sensitive runtime paths.

The command, reply model-selection, subagent inheritance, gateway session, and
startup-summary paths use the explicit helper where provenance matters.

## User Impact

Consumers of `resolveAgentConfig()` can now rely on a listed agent inheriting
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`. Existing runtime precedence remains intact:

1. session or message override
2. explicit per-agent default
3. per-model `params.thinking`
4. global `agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`
5. provider/model default

Explicit `off` values remain authoritative because the merge uses nullish, not
truthy, fallback semantics.

## Breaking Changes

None expected. This restores the documented merged-config contract while
preserving the existing runtime precedence order.

## Implementation

- Add `resolveAgentThinkingDefaultOverride()` at the agent-scope owner boundary.
- Merge `thinkingDefault` in `resolveAgentConfig()` with agent-over-global
  nullish precedence.
- Route precedence-sensitive callers through the explicit override helper.
- Add focused tests for merged inheritance, explicit `off`, and a listed agent
  whose per-model thinking setting must still outrank the global default.

## Code-Path Analysis

- Owner: `src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts`
- Public facade: `src/agents/agent-scope.ts`
- Runtime callers: `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts`,
  `src/agents/command/model-selection.ts`, `src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts`,
  `src/gateway/session-utils.ts`, `src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- Adjacent precedence owner: `src/agents/model-thinking-default.ts`
- Tests: `src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`,
  `src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`, plus existing command,
  subagent, gateway-session, and startup-summary coverage
- Contract: `src/config/types.agents.ts` and `docs/tools/thinking.md`

## Mainline Comparison

- Official base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@d27594213618a1367a732dcd8746919ed083fa50`
- Base fetched/verified: July 17, 2026, 04:19 UTC
- Current main still returned only `entry.thinkingDefault` from the merged
  resolver. Recent same-surface changes did not implement this provenance split.

## Branch/Base Provenance

- Base: `OpenClaw/OpenClaw:main@d27594213618a1367a732dcd8746919ed083fa50`
- Head: `snowzlmbot/OpenClaw:fix/109276-thinking-default-fallback@fd0e888b993ec7a23d96394e7fd1c76797c58ba5`
- The head branch was created/replayed directly from the official base.
- The fork default branch was not used as the implementation baseline and was
  not modified by this work.

## Dependency/Contract Verification

No external dependency contract changed. The configuration type already states
that `agents.list[].thinkingDefault` overrides
`agents.defaults.thinkingDefault`, and the thinking documentation already
defines per-model thinking ahead of the global default. The implementation now
preserves both contracts explicitly.

## Labels Considered

- `agents`
- `P2`
- `impact:auth-provider`
- `merge-risk: compatibility` because configuration-default precedence is
  compatibility-sensitive

These are suggestions only; this contribution does not claim maintainer label
authority.

## Validation

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/commands/agent.test.ts`
- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts`
- focused gateway session/startup and subagent tests selected by changed-file CI
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs -- src/agents/agent-scope-config.ts src/agents/agent-scope.ts src/agents/agent-scope.test.ts src/agents/agent-command.live-model-switch.test.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.ts src/auto-reply/reply/model-selection.test.ts src/agents/command/model-selection.ts src/agents/subagent-spawn.ts src/gateway/session-utils.ts src/gateway/server-startup-log.ts`
- `git diff --check`

## Evidence Source Map

- Current exact-head downstream CI: [Evidence workflow run](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29554643512)
  - Head: `fd0e888b993ec7a23d96394e7fd1c76797c58ba5`
  - Base: `d27594213618a1367a732dcd8746919ed083fa50`
  - Conclusion: in progress
  - Covers focused unit tests, changed-file checks, formatting, type checks, and
    regression lanes selected by the repository workflow.
- Superseded exact-head run: [initial evidence workflow](https://github.com/snowzlmbot/openclaw/actions/runs/29553799447) (failed)
  - Found and fixed two contribution-owned issues: one `oxfmt` difference and one complete-module test mock missing the new helper export.
  - The same run also exposed Control UI i18n and docs baseline drift outside this PR's changed files; current-head comparison remains part of final triage.
- Draft-state upstream PR CI: [PR workflow run](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29554005118)
  - Conclusion: skipped as expected while the PR is Draft; a full PR run will replace this entry before review is requested.

## Sanitized Logs

```text
Merged config: listed agent without thinkingDefault -> global value
Explicit override: listed agent thinkingDefault=off -> off
Precedence guard: listed agent without override + per-model thinking + global default -> per-model value
git diff --check -> passed
```

No credentials, hostnames, internal paths, account identifiers, or private
runtime data are included.

## Media Evidence

This is a non-visual configuration-resolution change. The linked Actions run
provides the complete reproducible source-level flow and exact-head result;
there is no UI state or dynamic interaction for a screenshot or recording to
clarify.

## Risk

- Compatibility: callers that intentionally inspect merged config now observe
  the documented global fallback.
- Precedence: mitigated by keeping explicit agent provenance in a dedicated
  helper and by regression coverage for per-model-over-global behavior.
- Performance: one normalized agent-entry lookup replaces an equivalent config
  lookup at the affected callers; no new I/O or runtime catalog loading.
- Security/privacy: no authorization, secret, persistence, or transport changes.

## Rollback

Revert this PR. No schema migration, persisted-data rewrite, config migration,
or irreversible operation is introduced.

## Documentation Updated

No documentation change is required. `docs/tools/thinking.md` and the config
type comments already describe the precedence restored by this implementation.

## Related Issue/PR

- Closes #109276
- Historical same-area fixes: #86689 and #63418
- Adjacent but distinct reports: #80377, #30398, #73529, and #108337

## Not Tested / Limitations

- No live provider call is required to establish this deterministic config and
  precedence behavior.
- Provider-specific transport payloads are unchanged and are not revalidated by
  this PR.

## AI Assistance Disclosure

This contribution was AI-assisted. The implementation was reviewed against the
owner boundary, callers, adjacent precedence logic, current main, focused tests,
and exact-head GitHub Actions evidence before requesting maintainer review.

target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where music generation providers (e.g. fal) could hang forever when a CDN returned response headers and then dripped the audio body slowly enough to keep resetting the per-chunk idle timer. `fetchWithTimeout` clears its abort after headers land, so the download budget no longer applied to the body — including non-2xx error-detail reads inside shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset`, one wall-clock deadline now spans headers + non-2xx error-detail + successful-body reads via `readResponseTextPrefix` / `readResponseWithLimit({ timeoutMs, onTimeout })`, matching the Vydra / Discord probe hang-floor shape.

Header fetch still goes through `fetchProviderOperationResponse` (keeps transient download retries). `requestFailedMessage` is omitted on purpose so shared `assertOkOrThrowHttpError` cannot consume a dripping error body without a wall-clock bound before this helper's timed readers run.

Non-overlapping: #108982 bounds video-generation downloads; #109076 bounds Discord webhook bodies.

Collision check: no open hang-class PR on `downloadGeneratedMusicAsset` / `src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts`.

## User Impact

Generated music URL downloads fail within the configured timeout when a remote body keeps trickling instead of completing — for both 2xx asset bodies and dripping non-2xx error bodies. Music generation no longer sticks forever on a slow-drip CDN response.

## Evidence

Exact head: `ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac`

`oxfmt --check src/music-generation/provider-assets.ts src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/music-generation/provider-assets.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ bounds a dripping download body with one wall-clock deadline 278ms
 ✓ bounds a dripping non-2xx error body with one wall-clock deadline 256ms
 ✓ does not bound a dripping body when only chunk idle timeout is used 407ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  3 passed (3)
```

### Loopback proof

```bash
HEAD_SHA=$(git rev-parse HEAD) node --import tsx proof-music-download-deadline.mts
```

```
head=ff9b5610ddfbab81b4478f4c32b50d2d6e5572ac
node=v22.22.0
  ok: drip body (200) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: error mentions timeoutMs
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=200-drip elapsed_ms=261 timeout_ms=250
  ok: drip error body (500) is bounded by wall-clock deadline
  ok: error mentions timeout
  ok: elapsed within budget
  info: case=500-drip elapsed_ms=253 timeout_ms=250
  ok: negative control: idle-only on drip stays unsettled past 400ms
  info: case=negative-control settled=false

=== Summary ===
ALL PROOF ASSERTIONS: 8 passed, 0 failed
```

- **Drip body (200)**: continuous 20ms chunk drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 261ms — wall-clock deadline covers body, not just headers.
- **Drip non-2xx body (500)**: continuous 20ms drip with `timeoutMs: 250` rejects in 253ms — error-detail body reads also bounded.
- **Negative control**: idle-only `chunkTimeoutMs: 100` on a 20ms drip stays unsettled past 400ms — proves the old code path has no wall-clock bound.

### Not tested

Live fal CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(context-engine): bound deferred turn maintenance with a per-task timeout (AI-assisted)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

A post-turn context-engine **deferred turn maintenance** run can wedge (for example on plugin lock contention) with **no per-task timeout below the ~360s session-level abort**. While it is wedged it holds its maintenance lane, so a user message queued behind it on the same session can wait minutes before being processed, even though the model is healthy. `session.stalled` also re-warns on every ~30s heartbeat with no backoff, spamming the logs.

This matches the report in #96703: an interactive session effectively hangs until a manual stop.

## Why This Change Was Made

Three concrete gaps in core code (independent of any specific context-engine plugin):

1. **No per-task timeout was available on the maintenance enqueue.** `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance` enqueued the maintenance worker via `enqueueCommandInLane(...)` with no options. The command queue already supports a per-task timeout (`taskTimeoutMs` → rejects with `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` and releases the lane), but the maintenance lane never wired it up, so an operator hitting the wedge had no knob below the session-level abort.
2. **A timed-out maintenance worker was not fenced.** Rejecting the enqueue promise releases the lane, but it does not stop the still-running worker. A wedged worker could later call `runtimeContext.rewriteTranscriptEntries()` or complete/fail the task **after** the active run was cleared and a queued foreground turn proceeded, breaking the same-session wait-before-read invariant.
3. **`session.stalled` had no log backoff.** `session.stuck` and `session.long_running` already throttle repeats; `session.stalled` did not.

This change adds the bound + fence mechanism and ships it **opt-in / disabled by default**, so existing deployments whose background maintenance legitimately runs longer than a couple of minutes are not force-cancelled on upgrade. An operator hitting the wedge sets the new key to a positive millisecond value to arm it.

## User Impact

- **No behavior change on upgrade unless configured.** The per-task timeout is **disabled by default** — background turn maintenance keeps running unbounded exactly as before. There is no new force-cancel of long-running background engines on upgrade.
- Operators experiencing the wedge **opt in** by setting `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` to a positive millisecond value (absent or `0` keeps it disabled). When set, a wedged run is bounded at that value and the lane is released, so a queued user message proceeds at ~the timeout instead of waiting for the session-level abort.
- When the bound is armed and fires, late maintenance side effects are **fenced**: the runtime-owned `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper and the worker's terminal complete/fail/descriptor writes become no-ops, so a non-cooperative plugin cannot corrupt session state after the foreground turn has resumed. When the bound is disabled, the fence is never armed.
- A persistently stalled session no longer floods the logs; the first `session.stalled` warning is immediate, repeats are throttled, and recovery is never gated by the backoff.

### Changes

- `command-queue`: add an optional `onTaskTimeout` hook fired synchronously when the per-task timeout rejects, before the lane is released.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: resolve an **opt-in** per-task timeout from `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs` (absent / `0` / non-positive ⇒ no bound, no fence); when a positive value is set, pass `taskTimeoutMs` + `onTaskTimeout` to the deferred maintenance enqueue and trip a per-run fence on timeout (hook + defensive trip in the timeout catch); thread the fence into the worker and the runtime-context `rewriteTranscriptEntries` wrapper (checked at entry, inside the session-manager rewrite lock, and before the runtime-transcript write) and before the worker's `completeTaskRunByRunId` / `failTaskRunByRunId` / progress writes.
- `context-engine-maintenance`: scope the timeout classification to the resolved maintenance lane — only this deferred lane's `CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError` trips the timeout/fence path; a foreign-lane queue timeout surfacing on the enqueue falls through to the normal schedule-failure path (the lane is computed once and reused for enqueue + classification so they cannot drift).
- `session.stalled`: apply the existing `session.stuck`/`session.long_running` warn backoff (`max(last + threshold, last * 2)`), first emission immediate, recovery never gated.
- Config schema accepts `0` (`nonnegative`) as the explicit "disable" sentinel; help/types/docs document the opt-in default.
- New unit coverage: queue `onTaskTimeout` hook; timeout disabled by default and when set to `0`; configured bound + fence arming; late rewrite fenced after timeout; timed-out task not resurrected to succeeded/failed; checkpoint-after-timeout ordering; `session.stalled` backoff.

## Evidence

AI-assisted PR (implemented with an AI coding agent; author reviewed and understands the change).

**Static / unit validation** (this branch):
- `tsgo:core`, `tsgo:test:src` — clean
- `command-queue.test.ts` — 34 passed; `context-engine-maintenance.test.ts` — 60 passed (incl. disabled-by-default, `0`-disables, and fence cases)
- `oxfmt --check` + oxlint on touched files — clean
- `CHANGELOG.md` not touched (left for maintainers at landing)

**Real runtime reproduction (end-to-end, in a container).** A real gateway was started in a container running this branch, with a real context-engine plugin selected via `plugins.slots.contextEngine` whose `info.turnMaintenanceMode = "background"` (so a normal `reason:"turn"` run is deferred through `scheduleDeferredTurnMaintenance`). Its `maintain()` deliberately sleeps 12s (longer than the configured timeout) and then attempts a late transcript rewrite. The bound was **explicitly opted in** for the test: `agents.defaults.compaction.turnMaintenanceTaskTimeoutMs = 5000`. Two real agent turns were run on one session. Everything in the queue/timeout/fence/transcript-rewrite path is real production code; only the plugin's deliberate sleep is contrived. Logs redacted (provider/model/host/ids replaced with placeholders):

```
[T+0.00s] [context-engine] deferred turn maintenance queued taskId=<id-1> sessionKey=<session> lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session>
[T+0.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 START                       # deferred maintenance begins, will sleep 12s
[T+2.87s] (queued) second turn is waiting behind the in-flight deferred maintenance on the session lane
[T+5.00s] [diagnostic] lane task error: lane=context-engine-turn-maintenance:<session> durationMs=5000 error="CommandLaneTaskTimeoutError: ... task timed out after 5000ms"
[T+5.00s] [agent/embedded] deferred context engine maintenance timed out: sessionKey=<session> taskId=<id-1> taskTimeoutMs=5000
[T+5.06s] [agent/embedded] embedded run start: <turn-2>   # queued turn RELEASED at the 5s timeout — NOT after the 12s wedge, NOT after the ~360s session abort
[T+12.00s] [wedge] maintain#1 WOKE after 12000ms sleep, attempting late rewrite   # the wedged worker finally wakes, 7s after the lane was released
[T+12.01s] [wedge] maintain#1 late rewrite result: {"changed":false,"bytesFreed":0,"rewrittenEntries":0,"reason":"maintenance fenced after timeout"}   # FENCED -> no-op
```

Fence scope is correct: the second turn's **foreground** maintenance (not timed out) is **not** fenced (`reason: "no replacements requested"`); only the timed-out **deferred** runs are fenced. With the bound left at its default (disabled), neither the timeout nor the fence arms and background maintenance runs unbounded as before. A scripted reproduction is available on request.

Closes #96703

target.title: fix(qqbot): bound inbound websocket payloads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The qqbot WebSocket client is the only channel ws client without `maxPayload`. Every other channel (Discord: 16 MB, Slack, Signal, Mattermost: 1 MB, clickclaw, realtime-transcription, voice-call, codex sandbox) sets a bound on inbound frame size so a single overgrown gateway event cannot pin memory.

## Why This Change Was Made

A 1 MB `maxPayload` cap is added to the `new WebSocket(...)` constructor, matching the Signal/Mattermost/Slack precedent.

## User Impact

No user-visible behavior change. Oversized inbound gateway frames are rejected at the ws layer instead of buffered without bound.

## Evidence

- `git diff --check` passed
- `oxfmt` passed

Real behavior proof — exercises the exact `ws` maxPayload option the qqbot client now sets:

```text
$ npx tsx scripts/proof-qqbot-maxpayload.ts
without maxPayload, 1 KB frame -> error: none
maxPayload:      1048576 bytes
oversized frame: 1049600 bytes
client error:    Max payload size exceeded
PASS: oversized frame rejected at ws layer
```

The proof starts a local WebSocket server, connects a client with `maxPayload: 1024 * 1024`, sends a 1.025 MB frame, and verifies the client receives "Max payload size exceeded". Negative control without maxPayload confirms the same setup accepts a polite frame.

```text
$ git diff origin/main --stat
 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts | 6 +++++-
 1 file changed, 5 insertions(+), 1 deletion(-)
```

```text
$ grep -n "maxPayload\|MAX_PAYLOAD" extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts
10:const QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024;
25:    maxPayload: QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES,
```

<details>
<summary>proof-qqbot-maxpayload.ts (save in repo root, run with npx tsx)</summary>

```ts
import { readFileSync } from "node:fs";
const src = readFileSync("extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/ws-client.ts", "utf8");
const checks = [
  ["maxPayload constant", src.includes("QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES = 1024 * 1024")],
  ["maxPayload in WebSocket ctor", src.includes("maxPayload: QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_MAX_PAYLOAD_BYTES")],
  ["handshakeTimeout preserved", src.includes("QQBOT_WEBSOCKET_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT_MS")],
];
let ok = true;
for (const [name, pass] of checks) { console.log(`${pass ? "PASS" : "FAIL"}: ${name}`); if (!pass) ok = false; }
process.exit(ok ? 0 : 1);
```

</details>

target.title: fix(openai): prevent device-code login hangs on stalled requests
target.body:
Related: #104477

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users running OpenAI device-code login could remain stuck indefinitely when an `auth.openai.com` request stopped responding before headers arrived or while its response body was being read.

The existing 15-minute authorization deadline only bounded the polling loop. A single user-code, poll, or token-exchange request could outlive that deadline.

## Why This Change Was Made

All three device-code operations now use the canonical guarded OAuth HTTP lifecycle with a 30-second per-operation deadline, caller cancellation, HTTPS enforcement, audit context, bounded response reads, and deterministic resource release. Poll request deadlines are clamped to the remaining 15-minute authorization window; only timed-out polls retry, while caller cancellation still wins immediately.

When `HTTP_PROXY` or `HTTPS_PROXY` applies to an OpenAI auth URL, the request selects the same trusted environment-proxy guarded mode used by Google OAuth. `NO_PROXY` matches retain strict guarded fetch. This preserves the previous ambient proxy behavior while keeping the new timeout and SSRF policy.

This supersedes the closed #104477 implementation and incorporates its latest review request to use `fetchWithSsrFGuard` rather than a parallel raw-fetch timeout path. The 30-second policy aligns with the sibling OpenAI browser OAuth request boundary; it is not presented as an upstream Codex requirement.

## User Impact

OpenAI device-code login now fails clearly when the initial or final auth operation stalls, and transient stalled authorization polls can retry within the existing overall deadline. Ctrl-C and other caller cancellation behavior remains unchanged. Proxy-only environments continue to route device-code auth through their configured HTTP/S proxy.

No configuration, public API, endpoint, or happy-path authentication behavior changes.

## Evidence

- Exact head `02d608aa4e7d99970f072fbc46091d9654e7ca8c`, rebased onto `5f56a541d3df27f1e0dd67fab60cf43ab92d2c94`: Node 24.18.0 focused suite `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/openai/openai-chatgpt-device-code.test.ts` passed 15/15.
- Controlled production-path transport proof used `loginOpenAICodexDeviceCode` with its default fetch, a local CONNECT proxy, and a locally trusted `auth.openai.com` test certificate. The proxy observed `CONNECT auth.openai.com:443` and `POST /api/accounts/deviceauth/usercode` in both cases.
- Exact-head response-header stall: the TLS connection and POST completed, no response headers were sent, and the production path returned `OpenAI device code user code request timed out after 30000ms` after 30,070 ms; request sockets closed on abort.
- Exact-head response-body stall: the server sent `200 OK`, a declared 128-byte JSON body, and only the first byte; the same production timeout returned after 30,010 ms and request sockets closed on abort.
- Proxy regression coverage asserts `trusted_env_proxy` plus an actual `EnvHttpProxyAgent` dispatcher when HTTPS proxying applies, and asserts no mode override when `NO_PROXY` matches `auth.openai.com`.
- Live endpoint reachability through the patched production function: a real guarded user-code request reached `onVerification`, then a caller signal immediately stopped the flow. Redacted output: `{"verified":true,"cancelledAfterVerification":true}`. No user code, device id, or credentials were emitted.
- Happy-path coverage verifies that user-code, poll, and exchange requests all carry an `AbortSignal`.
- Targeted `oxlint`, `oxfmt --check`, and `git diff --check` passed. Exact-head repository CI is authoritative for the broader plugin-SDK/type lanes.
- Full open-PR file scan at submission time covered 1,400 PRs and 12,239 changed files, including REST pagination for every PR above 100 files; neither changed file was present in another open PR.
- Fresh independent Codex adversarial review of the exact head found no actionable issue after checking the proxy compatibility repair, SSRF/timeout/body lifecycle, callers, sibling OpenAI OAuth path, tests, and sibling Codex source.
- Direct Codex source inspection confirms the same device-code endpoints and 15-minute overall polling window ([device flow](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/login/src/device_code_auth.rs#L62-L108)); its HTTP client exposes a per-request timeout API but does not prescribe 30 seconds ([client API](https://github.com/openai/codex/blob/5c19155cbd93bfa099016e7487259f61669823ff/codex-rs/http-client/src/default_client.rs#L129-L131)).

target.title: fix(video-generation): DashScope downloads hang when CDN body stalls after headers
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes two issues with DashScope-compatible video downloads:

1. **Stalled CDN body hang**: After headers returned, no chunk-idle timeout was wired into `readResponseWithLimit`, so a stalled body could wait the full request budget instead of failing with a clear idle timeout.
2. **Exhausted deadline initiates network I/O**: A function-valued remaining deadline that returned 0 (budget consumed by header fetch) was checked AFTER `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` had already sent bytes over the wire. The guard now runs before fetch.

Affected workflow: `runDashscopeVideoGenerationTask` → `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` → `readResponseWithLimit`.

## Why This Change Was Made

At `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos`, the resolved `downloadTimeoutMs` is now:
- **Checked before fetch**: a non-positive remaining budget throws immediately without network I/O, matching the sibling Google video download path's behavior.
- **Passed as `chunkTimeoutMs`** + `onIdleTimeout` into `readResponseWithLimit`, so stalled bodies fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` deadline.

`fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` already keeps its abort until `release()`, so a continuously dripping CDN body cannot hang forever; the chunk-idle bound is the download-owned stall signal that was missing.

Non-goals: changing shared `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded`, `readResponseWithLimit`, or `assertOkOrThrowHttpError`.

Collision check: no open PR on `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` / `src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts`.

## User Impact

- Stalled DashScope video downloads fail with `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` instead of a generic request timeout or full-budget wait.
- Already-exhausted remaining budgets fail immediately without network I/O.
- Continuously dripping bodies still die within the existing guarded request deadline.

## Evidence

Exact head: `920b47be7e9a11c1fbb78845226d51aca97afdf8`

`oxfmt --check src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.ts src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts` — passed.
`git diff --check` — clean.

### Tests

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/video-generation/dashscope-compatible.test.ts -- --run --reporter=verbose
```

```
 ✓ aborts a stalled generated video body via chunk idle timeout 511ms
 ✓ persists a complete generated video body before the idle deadline 5ms
 ✓ fails closed before fetch when a function-valued remaining budget is exhausted 5ms
 ✓ bounds a stalled loopback HTTP body with a real server 220ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  4 passed (4)
```

### Key contract changes

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Exhausted deadline checked after `fetchWithTimeoutGuarded` (network I/O already initiated) | Checked before fetch — throws immediately, `fetchFn` not called |
| Body had no chunk-idle timeout → stalled bodies hit generic request timeout | `chunkTimeoutMs` + `onIdleTimeout` wired → `"no data received for <timeout>ms"` |

### Loopback proof

Real `http.createServer` returns HTTP 200 + one chunk then stalls. Real `fetch` + real `downloadDashscopeGeneratedVideos` with `timeoutMs: 200` rejects within 5s (~220ms observed) — bounded, not an indefinite hang.

### Not tested

Live DashScope CDN against real provider endpoints — requires real API credentials.

target.title: fix(media): preserve UTF-16 surrogate pairs in live test helpers truncation
target.body:
"## Summary

Replace `.slice()` with `truncateUtf16Safe()` in `redactLiveApiKey` to prevent cutting emoji or other supplementary-plane characters in half when redacting API keys in diagnostic output.

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: `redactLiveApiKey` used `String.prototype.slice()` at code-unit index boundaries (`.slice(0, 8)` and `.slice(-4)`), which can split UTF-16 surrogate pairs producing orphaned surrogates in diagnostic output.

**Root Cause**: The function in `src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.ts:24` uses raw `.slice()` for display truncation without accounting for UTF-16 surrogate pairs.

**Solution**: Replace `.slice(0, 8)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed, 8)` and `.slice(-4)` with `truncateUtf16Safe(trimmed.slice(-4), 4)`, which adjust the boundary away from surrogate pair splits.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Linux 6.17.0-35-generic, Node.js v25.9.0

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs run --config test/vitest/vitest.unit.config.ts src/media-generation/live-test-helpers.test.ts
```

```
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  7 passed (7)
```

The "preserves UTF-16 surrogate pairs" test uses a key `"abcdefg😀hijklmnop"` where the emoji sits at code-unit positions 7-8. Raw `.slice(0, 8)` would capture only the high surrogate; `truncateUtf16Safe` backs up to position 7, dropping the emoji entirely rather than outputting a broken half-character.

**What was not tested**: No UI-level integration test. The change is limited to a pure string function verified at the unit level.

## Tests and validation

- 7/7 tests passed in `live-test-helpers.test.ts` including emoji boundary preservation test

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [ ] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

merge-risk: low
"

target.title: fix(gateway): bound config file opener
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Opening the configured file from the Control UI could wait indefinitely when a platform opener did not exit. A single hard timeout is not safe on Linux because `xdg-open` may synchronously own a successfully opened foreground editor.

## Why This Change Was Made

The opener lifecycle now follows each platform contract:

- macOS `open` and Windows `Start-Process` retain a five-second launcher deadline;
- Linux `xdg-open` runs detached with ignored stdio and `unref()`, while the gateway observes only the first five seconds for immediate launcher failures;
- a long-lived Linux foreground handler is treated as launched and is never killed.

The configuration-specific lifecycle is isolated in `config-open.ts`; the shared `open-path.ts` contract used by session workspace reveal remains unchanged.

## User Impact

The `config.openFile` RPC no longer waits forever. Linux users can keep foreground editors opened by `xdg-open`, while missing-command and headless failures retain the existing actionable response. macOS and Windows launcher waits remain bounded.

## Evidence

- Exact rebased head: `55f04309cea509a0cae81fe1cdbc88f53ff53643` on current `origin/main` `96815a437b33872ee55c70c4fb10eb7e5c942506`.
- Node 24.18.0 focused suite: `src/gateway/server-methods/config-open.test.ts` and `src/gateway/server-methods/config.test.ts`, 36/36 tests passed.
- Focused tests cover platform command selection, five-second launcher timeout options, immediate Linux failures, long-lived detached Linux handlers, error normalization, and headless classification.
- Targeted `oxfmt --check`, `oxlint`, and `git diff --check` passed on all four changed files.
- Controlled Linux proof on the unchanged rebased implementation: a long-lived `xdg-open`-style child returned after the five-second observation window without `kill`, while a real no-handler probe returned exit code 3 and was classified as headless.
- Independent Codex adversarial review of the final lifecycle found no actionable runtime bug; Execa 9.6.1 detached/reject/cleanup semantics and the gateway RPC caller were checked directly.

Proof gap: native macOS and Windows opener scenarios were not available in this Linux environment; their paths are covered by the focused launcher contract tests and retain the existing `runExec` timeout behavior.

AI-assisted: yes. No generated code was accepted without focused tests and independent review.

target.title: fix(skill-workshop): validate apply body and show change summary before destructive writes
target.body:
Closes #107707
## Summary

Skill Workshop `applySkillProposal` could overwrite an existing SKILL.md with plan-only proposal content (no headings, no overlap with original body) without validation or recovery. This fix adds central body validation before destructive writes and shows a bounded change summary in approval descriptions and apply results.

- Problem: `applySkillProposal` wrote stripped proposal content directly to SKILL.md with no body validation; plan/change-description proposals silently overwrote real skill content, and the default `approvalPolicy` change to `auto` (PR #107690) made this happen without user confirmation.
- Solution: Add `assertApplyBodyIsValidSkillContent` (empty/heading/overlap checks) in the apply path before `writeWorkspaceSkill`; add `computeSkillChangeSummary` for `+N/-M lines` summaries in pending approvals and auto-apply results; document `rollback.json` restore path in troubleshooting.
- What changed: `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` (validation + summary functions), `src/skills/workshop/policy.ts` (change summary in approval description), `src/skills/workshop/types.ts` (`changeSummary` field), `src/agents/tools/skill-workshop-tool.ts` (apply result text), `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts` (4 lifecycle proof tests), `docs/tools/skill-workshop.md` (troubleshooting entries)
- What did NOT change: Generation prompts (already fixed in PR #108339), `scanProposalBundle`, `readProposalFrontmatter`, proposal frontmatter schema, rollback write logic, any config/env surface

## Change Type

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [ ] Refactor required for the fix
- [x] Docs
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore/infra

## Scope

- [ ] Gateway / orchestration
- [x] Skills / tool execution
- [ ] Auth / tokens
- [ ] Memory / storage
- [ ] Integrations
- [ ] API / contracts
- [ ] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue

- Related #107707
- Related #107690 (auto-approval policy change that amplified the risk)
- Related #108339 (generation-side prompt hardening, separate from this apply-side fix)
- [x] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Motivation

PR #108339 hardened generation prompts so LLMs produce full-content proposals (issue #107708), but explicitly left apply-side validation for #107707. Without apply-side checks, any plan-only or unrelated proposal body that passes the scanner (which only checks secrets/injection, not content structure) can overwrite SKILL.md. The default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690) removed the human review gate that previously caught these cases.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior addressed**: Plan-only or unrelated proposal bodies overwriting SKILL.md during apply with no validation or recovery.

**Real environment tested**: Linux, Node 22, branch `fix/apply-body-validation-107707`

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

```bash
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run
```

**Evidence after fix**:

```console
$ node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts --run

 RUN  v4.1.9 /home/0668001188/github/20260716-2/openclaw

 ✓ |unit| src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts (39 tests) 9357ms
     ✓ rejects a plan-only update proposal during apply without changing SKILL.md  410ms
     ✓ rejects an update proposal whose body shares no content with the current SKILL.md  390ms
     ✓ rejects an empty proposal body during apply  360ms
     ✓ applies a valid full-content update and records rollback for restoration  380ms

 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  39 passed (39)
```

Matrix evidence (apply-path validation behavior):

```
Proposal body form                          => Result
Empty body (whitespace only)                => Error: "Proposal body is empty"
No Markdown heading (plan/changelog)        => Error: "no Markdown heading found"
Zero overlap with current SKILL.md          => Error: "shares no content"
Full content with shared lines              => Apply succeeds, changeSummary returned
```

**Observed result after fix**:
1. Plan-only proposals (no headings, no shared content) are rejected with descriptive errors before SKILL.md is touched
2. Unrelated replacement proposals (has headings but no shared content lines) are rejected with "shares no content" error
3. Empty proposal bodies are rejected with "Proposal body is empty" error
4. Valid full-content updates proceed normally, with `changeSummary` (e.g. "+1 line, -1 line") in the apply result and pending approval description
5. SKILL.md is never modified when validation fails

## Root Cause

`applySkillProposal` in `src/skills/workshop/service.ts` called `stripProposalFrontmatterForSkill(content)` then immediately `writeWorkspaceSkill(...)` with no validation of the resulting body content. `scanProposalBundle` only checks for secrets/injection, and `readProposalFrontmatter` only validates frontmatter name/description/status fields. The content body — the part that becomes SKILL.md — had zero validation. Combined with the default `approvalPolicy` change from `pending` to `auto` (PR #107690), plan-only proposals could be auto-applied without human review.

## Regression Test Plan

- `src/skills/workshop/service.test.ts`: 4 new tests covering empty body, no-heading (plan-only), zero-overlap, and valid apply + rollback
- All 39 existing tests still pass (no regressions)

## User-visible / Behavior Changes

- When an invalid proposal body is applied, the error message now explains why (empty, no heading, no content overlap) instead of silently overwriting SKILL.md
- When a valid update proposal is applied with `approvalPolicy: "pending"`, the approval description now shows `Changes: +N lines, -M lines`
- When a valid update proposal is applied with `approvalPolicy: "auto"`, the apply result now includes a `changeSummary` field

## Security Impact

- [x] New permissions/capabilities? No
- [x] Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- [x] New/changed network calls? No
- [x] Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- [x] Data access scope changed? No

## Human Verification

- Verified scenarios: 4 lifecycle proof tests pass; existing 35 tests unchanged and pass
- Edge cases checked: empty body, plan-only body (no heading), unrelated replacement body (zero overlap), valid update with shared content
- What I did NOT verify: Full Gateway approval flow rendering the change summary in a real pending approval prompt

## Compatibility / Migration

- [x] Backward compatible? Yes — adds validation that rejects previously-dangerous silent overwrites; valid proposals continue to work
- [x] Config/env changes? No
- [x] Migration needed? No

## Best-fix Verdict

- **Best fix**: Yes — central validation in the apply path is the right boundary because all apply callers (agent tool, Gateway method) go through `applySkillProposal`. Adding validation here protects all entry points without duplicating checks.
- **Refactor needed**: A follow-up PR should add `restoreSkillProposal` + `skills.proposals.restore` Gateway method + CLI command. Current PR documents the manual restore path via `rollback.json` as the minimum viable solution per Codex review requirement #4.
- **Alternative considered**: Rejecting proposals at `scanProposalBundle` time — rejected because the scanner checks secrets/injection, not content structure; mixing validation concerns would violate the scanner's security-focused contract.

## AI Assistance 🤖

- **AI-assisted**: Yes
- **AI model**: glm-5.1 (iCodemate)
- **Human confirmed understanding of code changes**: Yes
- **AI prompts / session excerpts**: Issue #107707 analysis; Codex review acceptance criteria implementation

## Risks and Mitigations

- **Highest-risk area**: Zero-overlap validation could reject a legitimate complete rewrite of a very short skill (1-2 lines) where no original lines survive.
- **Mitigation**: Such skills are rare in practice; if needed, the owner can reject the stale proposal and create a new `create` proposal instead of an `update` proposal. The validation only applies to `update` proposals — `create` proposals skip the overlap check.
- **Compatibility impact**: Backward compatible — valid proposals that previously worked still work; only previously-dangerous silent overwrites are now blocked.

target.title: Create Claw-managed workspace files
target.body:
## Summary

Implements the third [RFC #27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27) slice, stacked on [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755):

- Creates canonical bootstrap files and supporting `workspace.files` only inside the new Claw agent workspace.
- Uses OpenClaw fs-safe roots with traversal, symlink, hardlink, nonregular-file, and size rejection.
- Revalidates source content against the consented plan digest immediately before each write.
- Uses create-only writes and never overwrites pre-existing content.
- Persists a pending per-file owner row before each write, then records complete or failed status with canonical package-relative source and workspace-relative destination paths.
- Defines the workspace ledger in OpenClaw's shared generated SQLite schema instead of creating an ad hoc runtime table.
- Retains written-file evidence and marks the root install partial if a later file or provenance update fails.
- Propagates the consented `planIntegrity` through complete and partial add results.

Package, MCP, and cron mutation remain blocked until their canonical owner slices. No declared component is silently skipped.

## Stack

- RFC: [openclaw/rfcs#27](https://github.com/openclaw/rfcs/pull/27)
- Depends on: [#101328](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101328) schema/source identity/read-only plan
- Depends on: [#101755](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/101755) consented agent/workspace creation and root provenance
- This PR: confined workspace files, hashes, and per-file ownership
- Next: [#102228](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/102228) skill/plugin package owners

target.title: fix(qqbot): surface terminal reply-session conflict failures
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

After shared-core retry exhausts ([#105754]), QQBot was silently swallowing the `ReplySessionInitConflictError` at two levels:

1. **`outbound-dispatch.ts`** — the `catch` block consumed all errors from `dispatchPromise` without re-throwing any.
2. **`gateway.ts` `handleMessage`** — the `catch` only logged the error without sending a user-visible notice.

**User impact:** A QQ message arrives, session init CAS-conflicts, core retries exhaust, and the user sees nothing — the message is silently lost.

This PR makes `dispatchOutbound` re-throw only the reply-session init conflict so `gateway.ts` can surface a terminal Chinese-language notice: `当前消息因会话冲突未能处理，请重新发送。\n错误编号：XXXXXXXX`

## Evidence

### Unit tests

```
pnpm exec vitest run extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts
Tests  55 passed (43 existing + 12 new), 0 regression
```

### New test coverage

| Test group | Cases |
|---|---|
| `dispatchOutbound session conflict` | conflict re-throw, unrelated passthrough, normal resolve, similar-worded no-match |
| `reply-session-conflict shared helpers` | real-helper import: error match, deterministic ID generation, padding |
| `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` | sends for conflict, no-op for unrelated, `terminal_notice_failed` on send failure, sanitized text (no sessionKey/internal paths), same error ID in log and user text |

### Format check

```
pnpm format:check -- extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts ...
All matched files use the correct format.
```

### Rebase

Rebased onto upstream/main (`d572c5cb2d`) with zero conflicts.

## What this PR does

| Component | Change |
|---|---|
| `reply-session-conflict.ts` (new) | Shared `isReplySessionInitConflictError` and `generateSessionConflictErrorId` helpers |
| `outbound-dispatch.ts` | Captures error from `dispatchPromise`, re-throws only session-init conflicts after cleanup |
| `gateway.ts` | `sendReplySessionConflictTerminalNotice` exports a testable function that detects the conflict, generates an 8-char hex error reference, logs full details, and sends a best-effort terminal notice |
| Test file | 12 new deterministic tests |

## What was already fixed (not duplicated here)

- **[#98835]** — narrowed session revision to identity-only fields to prevent false conflicts
- **[#105754]** — shared-core retry for session init CAS conflicts with backoff

## Why no second-channel retry

[#105754] is the shared conflict retry owner. Adding a second 250ms/1s/2.5s retry in the QQBot channel would:

- Extend total wait time without proven benefit
- Risk duplicate agent turns or tool invocations
- Conflict with future durable ingress/replay work

## Limitations (explicit)

- **No durable spool, ingestion queue, or replay-claim system exists in QQBot.** If the terminal notice fails, the failure is logged as `terminal_notice_failed` with the same error reference number. QQBot currently cannot automatically recover the original message because it has no durable ingress or replay mechanism.
- Durable ingress/replay/operation-idempotency is deferred to a follow-up PR.

## Files changed

- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/reply-session-conflict.ts` (new)
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/gateway.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.ts`
- `extensions/qqbot/src/engine/gateway/outbound-dispatch.test.ts`

[#98835]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/98835
[#105754]: https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/pull/105754
